title: The problem and the promised outcome

learningSteps.purpose: Understand the problem and the promised outcome.
learningSteps.question: What specific delivery failures is Mission Rail fixing, and what observable outcome would prove the replacement works?
learningSteps.explanation: Start by separating the pain we experienced from the product outcome we are committing to deliver.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: If the problem and outcome are vague, the new system can reproduce the old complexity with cleaner names.

title: The rules that constrain every design

learningSteps.purpose: Understand the rules that constrain every design.
learningSteps.question: Which principles are non-negotiable, and where would you push back if implementation made the rail slower or more complicated?
learningSteps.explanation: These principles decide which safety guarantees remain and which forms of ceremony must disappear.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: The principles are the test for future design decisions that the architecture cannot predict today.

title: Identity and the pure mission rail

learningSteps.purpose: Understand identity and the pure mission rail.
learningSteps.question: Why must canonical identity and next-action calculation be separate, pure package responsibilities?
learningSteps.explanation: Canonical identity answers what exact thing is being discussed; the pure rail answers the one legal next action without performing effects.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This boundary prevents filesystem, model, or host behavior from changing the meaning of mission state.

title: Guided Review as the human steering surface

learningSteps.purpose: Understand guided review as the human steering surface.
learningSteps.question: At which moments should Guided Review appear, and what information must it provide for you to make a meaningful decision?
learningSteps.explanation: Guided Review lets the human understand, challenge, and steer plans, exact code, and QA without reading agent transcripts.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This is how autonomy remains understandable instead of turning the human into either a bottleneck or a spectator.

learningSteps.purpose: Understand deterministic history and reusable lanes.
learningSteps.question: How do deterministic replay and stable Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie lanes prevent completed work from becoming stranded or ambiguous?
learningSteps.explanation: The store owns replayable history while lane lifecycle owns assignment, reconciliation, and return-to-ready decisions.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: Durable state and reusable workspaces address two of the most expensive failures in the original system.

learningSteps.question: Why should Mission Control display projections rather than calculate or mutate mission state itself?
learningSteps.explanation: The host performs Git, filesystem, process, signer, and agent effects; projection turns canonical state into readable status without becoming another workflow engine.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: Keeping effects and presentation outside the pure kernel makes the system portable and testable.

title: Who decides, who acts, and when work stops

learningSteps.purpose: Understand who decides, who acts, and when work stops.
learningSteps.question: Which decisions remain human, which transitions should be automatic, and what conditions genuinely justify parking a team?
learningSteps.explanation: Seat contracts preserve specialized responsibility while green signals should move routine work automatically.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This is the core balance between trustworthy governance and the speed you want from the team.

title: Track layers take trucks to work

learningSteps.purpose: Understand track layers take trucks to work.
learningSteps.question: What does Epic Wheels Up authorize once, and what material changes would still require the team to return to you?
learningSteps.explanation: The replacement rail is built in Track-Layer Mode under one bounded Epic Wheels Up decision; it is not forced to ride the defective system it replaces.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This construction model is what converts a large architecture into autonomous progress without abandoning human control.

learningSteps.purpose: Understand issues as executable construction packets.
learningSteps.question: What must every issue packet contain so a fresh team can implement it without improvising hidden contracts?
learningSteps.explanation: Each issue must carry enough exact scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria, paths, and validation information for a team to act without rediscovering the architecture.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: The issue graph is where architectural intent becomes repeatable team execution.

title: Portable execution and selective legacy extraction

learningSteps.purpose: Understand portable execution and selective legacy extraction.
learningSteps.question: What should remain invariant across AI hosts, and what evidence should justify extracting old code instead of rebuilding it?
learningSteps.explanation: Seat meaning remains stable across Factory, Codex, Copilot, and local models, while old code is harvested only when it fits the new boundary cleanly.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This prevents both host lock-in and accidental reconstruction of the legacy ball of twine.

learningSteps.question: Does this sequence prove the riskiest assumptions early enough, and are any dependencies ordered incorrectly?
learningSteps.explanation: The flights build identity first, then the pure rail, storage and lanes, host composition, and finally the thin CLI and proving issue.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: A sound architecture can still fail if its implementation order creates unnecessary coupling or delays the first real proof.

title: The proof and your GO decision

learningSteps.purpose: Understand the proof and your go decision.
learningSteps.question: Would the first-flight evidence convince you Mission Rail is real, and what must change in this architecture before you give Epic Wheels Up?
learningSteps.explanation: The architecture succeeds only when a cold Hill carries one curated issue from intake through visible QA and draft PR while returning the lane to ready.
learningSteps.whyItMatters: This checkpoint turns the document review into a concrete decision about starting the new rail.
